primitives.name: Static AST Query Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model (a) Static layer: GraphQL AST parsing with checks for query depth, alias overloading, batching, circular queries, directives, payload inflation, and SSRF patterns.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q': 'GraphQL query string', 'AST(Q)': 'Abstract Syntax Tree of Q', 'depth(Q)': 'integer, maximum nesting depth', 'alias_count(Q)': 'integer, number of aliases', 'batch_size(Q)': 'integer, number of operations'}
primitives.assumptions: Queries are well-formed and parseable into AST. Static rules are sufficient to block known attack vectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When query depth exceeds threshold or alias count exceeds limit

primitives.name: LLM Schema Threshold Generator
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) LLM layer: an LLM generates schema-specific thresholds and per-field complexity scores (the paper's novel claim — static ceilings alone are too blunt).
primitives.assumptions: LLM can generalize schema-specific complexity beyond static rules. Attackers may evade static thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When static thresholds fail to capture nuanced query behavior

layer2.mapping: LLM-derived thresholds act as learned kernel weights in a dynamic complexity model.
layer2.telemetry: Per-field complexity scores and schema-specific thresholds

primitives.verbatim_quote: (c) SQLi / OS-injection classifiers: SBERT all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings (384-dim) concatenated with handcrafted features (special-char counts, keyword counts); 1D CNN with filters 128/256/512, kernel size 3, batch-norm + max-pool; dense 256, dropout 0.5, sigmoid output; Adam lr 0.001, binary cross-entropy, ≤20 epochs, batch 32, early stopping patience 5.

primitives.assumptions: Injection patterns are learnable from labeled datasets. Embeddings and features are discriminative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When static and LLM layers do not definitively classify query

The layered architecture combines static AST validation as a hard gate, LLM-generated thresholds as soft advisories, and neural classifiers for injection detection. The static AST layer ensures syntactic correctness and enforces hard limits on query complexity. The LLM layer introduces schema-aware thresholds that adapt to domain-specific query structures, mitigating false positives from overly rigid rules. Neural classifiers provide robustness against evasion techniques by learning from large-scale labeled datasets. Each layer operates in a distinct regime: AST for syntax, LLM for semantics, and CNN for pattern recognition. Failure modes include LLM hallucination, classifier drift, and adversarial query obfuscation. The system's resilience depends on the integrity of the training data and the fidelity of the AST parser.
